    \caption{Aligned panels share the coupling axis $J$. Panel (a) shows the fingerprint separation from exact diagonalisation with synthetic finite-shot sampling overlaid (data source ED-N13). Panel (b) shows the half-cut entanglement entropy $S_{\mathrm{vN}}$ and the required bond dimension $\chi_{\mathrm{req}}$ from exact diagonalisation at $n \in \{8, 10, 12\}$ (data source ED-N11), drawn as individual curves per system size. Panel (c) continues $\chi_{\mathrm{req}}$ to $n = 20$ with TEBD on an explicitly marked instance sequence (data source TEBD-N14), with $\chi_{\mathrm{req}}$ reported at the $10^{-4}$ discarded-weight convention under a per-gate truncation tolerance of $10^{-12}$. The figure supports the operating-envelope statement for tested distinct-weight instances: inside the readable coupling range the fingerprint separates while the simulation cost stays small and roughly $n$-independent, and the cost rises outside that range. Tested sizes are proof of principle. The figure does not establish hardness of any kind, and it does not establish an asymptotic scaling law in $n$.}
